acceptance_signals: Governed session start captures an immutable privacy-bounded task baseline before implementation writes and fails closed on overwrite, unclassified paths, unstable capture, unsafe paths, or task binding drift.
The installed package owns the baseline implementation while the prior internal script remains a compatibility wrapper rather than a second policy implementation.
Completion reports exact unchanged pre-existing excluded identities as visible preserved non-owned findings that do not block otherwise verified completion.
Any changed, added, removed, renamed, copied, re-layered, newly excluded, unclassified, malformed, missing, or stale baseline identity blocks completion.
A missing valid task-start baseline preserves the existing strict raw-scope completion behavior for older sessions and direct evidence inspection.
Native MCP task completion and CLI completion apply the same baseline-aware policy without contradictory raw-scope prechecks.
Baseline records remain local, hash-only, repository-relative, immutable, and non-authorizing; they contain no raw patch, content, credential, environment, host, process, or human identity.
Existing evidence freshness, validation command identity, explicit platform shell execution, timeout, validation mutation detection, and authority boundaries remain unchanged.
Focused fixture tests cover start capture, rollback, collision, preserved exclusion, all material excluded-path drift modes, fallback strict behavior, MCP parity, and handoff freshness.
Affected user guidance, durable contracts, current status, and dated session evidence describe the integrated journey and its limits.
Focused and full unit tests, exact task validation, repository validation, and git diff checks pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-d1d3bd5ccbe748e8a1c5d6c2862e98e3 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Promote the existing deterministic task-start scope-baseline implementation into the installed AgentGov package and connect it to the governed start and completion journey. Starting a separately admitted task must capture one immutable local baseline before implementation writes. Completion may treat only exact unchanged pre-existing exclusions as visible non-owned preserved findings; every changed, added, removed, renamed, re-layered, unclassified, malformed, missing, or stale exclusion must fail closed. Tasks without a valid start baseline retain the current strict completion behavior. Native MCP completion must use the same completion policy instead of a contradictory raw-scope precheck. Preserve the already implemented shell-aware validation changes in overlapping files without retroactively verifying the predecessor task.

items: Capturing after implementation begins would launder earlier drift, so capture must be bound to the separately confirmed session-start transition.
A predictable baseline path could collide with stale local state; overwrite must remain forbidden and start must fail atomically.
Mapping preserved exclusions into completion could accidentally hide changed or re-layered work unless every exact Git-layer identity and both rename or copy endpoints are compared.
The native MCP completion path currently performs raw scope prechecks; removing only those checks must not bypass the baseline-aware completion assessment.
Promoting an internal prototype could create two policy implementations; the script must delegate to the installed package.
The development-evidence files already contain an unfinished admitted shell-runner repair; this task must preserve that behavior and explicitly validate the combined state.
A baseline file is local evidence, not an exception, task ownership transfer, semantic acceptance, Git authority, or release authority.
Reviewed assumption: The existing task-start baseline implementation and fixture evidence are a valid reusable deterministic mechanism.
Reviewed assumption: Each newly started task has a unique task identifier and one immutable local baseline path.
Reviewed assumption: Untracked local AgentGov state remains excluded by the canonical Git snapshot contract.
Reviewed assumption: The selected completion state names remain needs_evidence and verified; no new Kernel state is required.
Reviewed unknown: Performance on unusually large dirty worktrees remains unproven and will stay a documented limit.
Reviewed unknown: Old already-active sessions cannot gain a trustworthy pre-write baseline retroactively and must retain strict behavior.

title: Integrate preserved-exclusion baselines into governed completion
